purpose: Design of the orchestrator pattern for start-design, start-plan and start-requirements skills, including the shared context-gathering framework, responsibility split, failure handling and per-skill collection matrices.
summary: Overview of orchestrator-pattern construction for three create-style skills
Responsibility split between orchestrator, document search, code-collection agent, authoring, AI review and post-processing
Shared context-gathering framework: document search via query-db skills in main context, code exploration via general-purpose agent
Result handoff via return values without session directories, and inline prompt templates for agents
Collection order and integration sequence diagram
Failure handling: stop and report on search failure, not-performed search or agent error; zero results are valid
Per-skill design: start-design inputs, start-plan phases and matrix, start-requirements agent matrix and reverse-engineering sequence
Existing components reused by the design
Rationale for not using session directories
tasks: Designing or modifying start-design, start-plan or start-requirements skills
Implementing context gathering in create-style skills
Deciding where document search versus code exploration runs
Defining agent prompt templates and return-value contracts
